blocks.heading: Effective communication
blocks.text: Effective communication occurs when the intended message reaches the intended receiver and is understood as intended. Sending a message is not sufficient evidence that this happened. Business communication coordinates work, explains objectives, supports decisions and maintains relationships with staff, customers and suppliers. An accurate production instruction can still fail if it arrives after the work is completed or uses language the receiver does not understand. Feedback helps test understanding, especially where the message requires action. Communication should therefore fit the audience, purpose, urgency and need for a record. Effectiveness does not require the receiver to agree with every proposal: a worker can understand an unwelcome change clearly and still object. Managers should distinguish disagreement from misunderstanding and allow appropriate questions.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Owa Bakery changes tomorrow’s start time but sends the notice to an account some staff cannot access. Writing the correct time has not ensured effective communication. The manager must reach the affected staff before the change and confirm understanding, reducing late arrivals and disrupted preparation.
